messages.text: Buttler: McCullum can go 'all in' on Cricket World Cup without Test role

metadata.summary: Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.
metadata.content: Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances Brendon McCullum left his role as England Test coach in July; Jos Buttler believes the move has allowed the New Zealander to focus solely on helping England win the Cricket World Cup; Buttler has been ruled out of the upcoming Pakistan white-ball tour due to injury Tuesday 29 September 2026 15:39, UK Image: Jos Buttler says Brendon McCullum (pictured) is 'all in' on helping England win the Cricket World Cup in 2027 Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter. McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July , with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor , but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats. That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka , raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019. messages.text: Kick It Out receives record number of discrimination reports

metadata.summary: Kick It Out received a record 1,744 discrimination reports across professional football, grassroots, and online during the first year of its Football United strategy.
metadata.content: Kick It Out receives record 1,744 discrimination reports in first year of Football United strategy | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kick It Out receives record 1,744 discrimination reports in first year of Football United strategy Kick It Out's Year One Impact Report was published on Tuesday as the organisation attempts to make football more inclusive and representative; Kick It Out says the increase in reports should not be viewed solely as a deterioration in football's culture Tuesday 29 September 2026 13:18, UK Kick It Out received a record 1,744 discrimination reports across professional football, grassroots, and online during the first year of its Football United strategy. The organisation says a rise in anti-immigrant language contributed to the increase, while improved reporting relationships with groups including Her Game Too, The Frank Soo Foundation and Football v Homophobia also gave more people confidence to report incidents. More than 100 reports were received through those new channels during the 2025/26 season. Kick It Out says the increase in reports should not be viewed solely as a deterioration in football's culture, pointing to greater confidence among communities to report discrimination and improved relationships with partner organisations. The number of reporting partnerships is expected to increase during the 2026/27 season.
